title: Pradhan's Old Post Praising Wangchuk Goes Viral Amid Hunger Strike Standoff
excerpt: An old social media post by Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan appreciating Sonam Wangchuk and his wife has resurfaced as the activist enters the 26th day of his hunger strike demanding the minister's resignation over the NEET paper leak.
body:
• An old social media post by Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan praising Sonam Wangchuk and his wife has gone viral amid Wangchuk's ongoing hunger strike demanding Pradhan's resignation.
  • Wangchuk has been on an indefinite hunger strike since June 28, now entering its 26th day, over NEET paper leak irregularities — and was moved to a private hospital after a Delhi High Court order.
  • Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh reportedly assured Wangchuk that the government would "positively consider" Pradhan's resignation.
  • The protest has drawn global solidarity, with demonstrations held in New York, San Jose, London, and Dublin.

An old social media post by Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in which he posed alongside climate activist Sonam Wangchuk and his wife, Dr. Gitanjali Angmo, and wrote that he "appreciated their passion" has resurfaced and gone viral — a bitter irony given that Wangchuk is now entering the 26th day of an indefinite hunger strike demanding Pradhan's resignation.

The post, dating back to a time when the minister and the Ladakh-based educator shared a cordial relationship, has been widely reshared on X and other platforms. Users have highlighted the stark contrast between Pradhan's earlier praise and the current standoff, in which Wangchuk accuses the minister of failing to ensure accountability over the NEET-UG paper leak that affected millions of students.

From Praise to Protest

Wangchuk, the 59-year-old engineer and education reformist who inspired the Bollywood film 3 Idiots, began his hunger strike at Jantar Mantar on June 28 in solidarity with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical youth-led movement that grew out of a judge's remarks calling unemployed young Indians "cockroaches." The primary demand: that Pradhan resign over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak in May, which led to the exam's cancellation and a retest that left millions of aspirants in limbo.

https://x.com/CJP_for_India/status/2079993270244159530

"He is passionate about education. When he came to know about the social media movement and the discontent of the youth, he connected with the issue. It all happened in an organic way."

— Dr. Gitanjali Angmo, Wangchuk's wife, to The Hindu

Over three-and-a-half weeks, Wangchuk has lost over nine kilograms. His deteriorating health prompted Delhi Police to move him to Safdarjung Hospital on July 18, a step his wife described as "illegal detention." The Delhi High Court subsequently allowed his transfer to a private hospital.

Government Engagement and Shifting Demands

On July 22, Wangchuk said Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh had visited him in hospital and assured him the government would "positively consider" Pradhan's resignation. The ministers also reportedly promised to look into compensation for families of students who died by suicide amid the exam crisis.

Earlier, on July 20, Wangchuk released a handwritten note listing three conditions for ending his fast: that the government accept responsibility for education system lapses; that CJP leaders be allowed to meet MPs in Parliament; or that political leaders visit him and offer assurances on raising education accountability in the monsoon session. His conditions no longer explicitly mention Pradhan's resignation — a shift some have characterized as a U-turn, though supporters say the core demand remains unchanged.

International Solidarity and Parliamentary Impact

The protest has moved well beyond Jantar Mantar. On July 21, the CJP's "Sansad Chalo" march to Parliament disrupted the monsoon session's opening day, forcing repeated adjournments in both houses. Opposition lawmakers staged walkouts, and some MPs met protesters outside the Parliament complex.

"Our protests sent a clear message, whether in New York or London, San Jose or Dublin: India's students deserve to be treated with fairness and dignity."

— Hindus for Human Rights, in a statement

Internationally, activists from Hindus for Human Rights held demonstrations at the Mahatma Gandhi statue in New York's Union Square, in San Jose, outside the Indian High Commission in London, and at the Indian Embassy in Dublin. The Wall Street Journal covered the movement, describing how the hunger strike had galvanized India's largest youth protest in years against the Modi government.

What's Next

With the monsoon session underway and opposition parties pressing the government, the viral old post is a sharp reminder of how rapidly the political landscape has shifted. Congress has formally backed the demand for Pradhan's resignation, and celebrities including Sonakshi Sinha, Anurag Kashyap, and Naseeruddin Shah have spoken in support.

Wangchuk remains hospitalized but has vowed to continue fasting until student leaders meet parliamentarians or lawmakers visit him. As the standoff enters its fourth week, the government faces mounting pressure from the streets, the courts, and the opposition to address the education accountability crisis.
image_caption: Sonam Wangchuk, the Indian engineer, educator and climate activist. Wangchuk is on the 26th day of an indefinite hunger strike demanding Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over NEET paper leak irregularities.
